title: The 10 Best Speed Squares
subtitle: Speed squares, rafter squares and layout squares for framing and woodworking, ranked from live Amazon data.
intro: A speed square marks square and angled cuts, guides your circular saw and lays out rafters. We ranked 10 best-sellers from Swanson, Johnson Level, Klein Tools and value brands on rating, review volume and features (aluminum construction, scribe notches, rafter guides and multi-square packs).
data_source: Amazon product listings on the data_captured date. Prices, ratings and review counts change daily; check the listing before relying on a number.

scoring.review_age_weighting: Listings under 24 months old with at least 30 reviews have their review count multiplied by min(2, 24 / age in months, age floored at 6) before scoring; older listings are unchanged. Listing age is Amazon's Date First Available, or an estimate from the ASIN when the listing does not show it.

avoid.name: ALLWIN 7-Inch Aluminum Rafter Square, Double-Sided Engraved Scales (AL-SJC25)
avoid.flag: Claims it works as a level, with no vial
avoid.verdict: A cheap rafter square that claims it replaces a level and lasts three times longer, with no vial or test behind either claim.
reasons: It says it 'acts as a level', but nothing in the listing describes a level vial. The Johnson square that does work as a level has one.
It claims '0.1mm precision' and a '3X longer lifespan than stamped squares' without a standard or test.
It's rated 4.6 stars on 417 reviews. The Swanson T0118 costs less, and the Swanson S0101 costs a few dollars more with 17,328 reviews.

buyers_guide.a: Marking square and 45-degree lines on boards, guiding a circular saw for square cuts, and laying out rafter angles. It's the most-used layout tool on a framing job.
The 7-inch fits a tool belt and covers 2x lumber. A 12-inch square spans wider boards and is better for stair stringers and wide rafters.
Die-cast markings are molded into the square and can't wear off. Laser-etched markings are crisp but can fade with heavy use.
Notches at set intervals let you hold a pencil in place and slide the square along a board to draw a line parallel to the edge.

buyers_guide.q: Do I need the Blue Book?
buyers_guide.a: Only for rafters. It explains how to use the degree and pitch scales to mark common, hip, valley and jack rafters.
